title: 48 Hours in Lisbon on a Budget (What I'd Do Again)
creator: Wandering Wren
description:
Two days in Lisbon: trams, pastéis de nata, the best free viewpoint in the city, and one restaurant I'd skip.

Where I stayed: a guesthouse in Graça (not sponsored, just loved it)
Camera: Fujifilm X-S20
Music: Artlist

Places mentioned:
Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
Time Out Market
LX Factory
Belém

sentences.t: Good morning from Lisbon, it's seven a m, and I'm already sweating, which is a great sign.
Part of this video is sponsored by Airalo.
So I've got two days here and a pretty tight budget, so I'm going to show you exactly what I did and what it cost.
First stop, breakfast, which in Lisbon means a pastel de nata and a tiny coffee standing at the counter.
This whole thing was two euros twenty, and it's the best two euros I've spent all year.
The custard is still warm, and the top is that slightly burnt caramel, oh, that's so good.
Okay, so from here I'm taking the famous tram twenty eight up to the castle.
Now, real talk, the tram is iconic, but the line at the first stop is about an hour long by nine a m.
My tip is to walk two or three stops up the route and get on there, it's way less crowded.
And it's included in the day pass, which is around seven euros for unlimited metro, tram and bus.
We're climbing up through Alfama right now, and the streets are so narrow I could reach out and touch the laundry.
Okay, I got off near the top, and I'm skipping the castle itself, because it's fifteen euros and honestly the views are just as good for free.
I'm heading to Miradouro da Senhora do Monte instead, which is the highest viewpoint in the city.
And here it is.
That's the whole city, the river, the bridge, everything, and it costs nothing.
There's a guy playing guitar over there, and a couple of people having a picnic, and I could stay here all day.
For lunch I went to the Time Out Market, which everyone recommends, and I have mixed feelings.
The food is good, but it's loud, it's packed, and it's more expensive than the little tascas around the corner.
So afternoon of day one, I found one of those tascas, and the lunch special was soup, grilled fish, a glass of wine, and coffee for eleven euros.
Eleven, I'm not joking.
Day two, I took the train out to Belém, which is about twenty minutes along the river.
This is where the famous monastery is, and the tower, and the original pastel de nata bakery.
And I'm sorry to the breakfast place from yesterday, but these are better.
They give you cinnamon and powdered sugar on the side, and the pastry is somehow even flakier.
In the afternoon I went to LX Factory, which is an old industrial complex turned into shops, cafes, and a huge bookshop in an old printing hall.
I could have spent my whole budget in that bookshop, it was dangerous.
For sunset I went back up to a viewpoint, a different one this time, and just watched the city turn orange.
So all in, two days, food, transport and a couple of museums, I spent about ninety euros, not including where I stayed.
Lisbon is one of those cities that rewards you for walking and for being curious.
Let me know where I should go next, and I'll see you there.
